factsAccepted: Revenue grew 35% ($5.9M->$8.0M) but marketing spend grew ~117% ($1.2M->$2.6M) to achieve it. Spend is growing far faster than revenue, indicating worsening acquisition efficiency hidden behind a healthy-looking top-line growth rate.

Blended CAC rose from ~$38 to ~$61 (+60%) while AOV stayed flat at ~$72. At 60% gross margin a $72 order yields ~$43 gross profit, so a $61 CAC leaves first-order contribution negative before shipping and returns - the newest customers likely lose money on the first order and must repeat to become profitable.

12-month repeat-purchase rate is declining every cohort: 2022 42%, 2023 35%, 2024 28%. The exact mechanism (the repeats) that is supposed to rescue the negative first-order economics is weakening at the same time CAC rises. The two trends compound against the marginal customer.

~80% of new customers come from two paid platforms with rising CPMs. Doubling spend would push further into the same saturating channels, where marginal CAC typically rises above blended CAC - so the $61 figure likely understates the cost of the next customer at doubled spend. Marginal CAC at scale has not been modeled.
